URL: https://www.survation.com/labour-draw-level-with-reform-in-starmers-last-days-how-much-improvement-can-burnham-make/
Retrieved 2026-07-19 via Exa full fetch. Survation, published 2026-07-17 13:22 BST. Fieldwork 10-14 July 2026, 2,057 UK adults. Changes vs 17 June poll.

Labour draw level with Reform in Starmer's last days.
- Westminster voting intention: Labour 24% (+5, largest single upward movement since 2024 GE), Reform UK 24% (-3, lowest since weeks after May 2025 locals), Conservatives 21% (+1), Lib Dems 11% (-1), Greens steady. Labour's highest with Survation since 20 Nov 2025.
- Leader-prompted framing: Labour (Burnham) 24%, Reform (Farage) 24%, Con (Badenoch) 20% — naming Burnham makes little/no difference (he was already seen as de-facto leader).
- Starmer departs most disliked of five leaders tested: 22% like / 55% dislike (net -33). Farage -18, Polanski -21, Davey -3. Badenoch only leader in positive territory (+4).
- 38% picked Starmer as most "out of touch" (highest any leader on any trait). On strong leadership Starmer last of three (16%), behind Farage (24%) and Badenoch (22%).
- Party feeling: 20% feel closest to Labour, Reform 18%, Con 17%; 21% feel close to no party. Labour net like -16 (worse than Reform -11, Con -6).
